assign.request: Port three more MIT Codrops demos: a menu/navigation effect framed in the paging vocabulary (which mechanism), an image or grid transition, a hover-driven layout change. Add to the hub's DEMOS and children. Prove with ui-test at four widths and reduced-motion.
assign.now: scoping - read round-3.md, requirements.md, round-2.md, codrops readme, paging mechanism vocabulary
steps: read briefs + round 1/2 rules + paging mechanism vocabulary
shortlist + license-check candidate repos (github MIT search)
read source of 3 chosen repos, decide substitutions
wire into codrops hub (DEMOS + children + table)

log.msg: Licence pass (same method as rounds 1-2: api.github.com/search/repositories?q=org:codrops+license:mit, then the actual LICENSE file, never the badge). Shortlisted via keyword search (menu, grid, accordion): ExpandingRoundedMenu, MakeWayGridEffect, GridZoom, InlineMenuLayout, MenuThumbStackAnimation. Read LICENSE for the three picked - ExpandingRoundedMenu, GridZoom, MakeWayGridEffect - all genuine MIT (Codrops 2009-2021), READMEs clean (no redistribution caveat, images credited to Unsplash only).

Picked: ExpandingRoundedMenu (a pill-shaped top-bar menu that grows in place into a full nav panel on click) for the menu/nav slot - maps to this realm's own expand mechanism (opens below, in place, item grows, nothing else moves) since it never navigates or moves the surrounding content. GridZoom (click a grid tile, it scales up via FLIP into a detail panel, other tiles fade) for the image/grid transition slot. MakeWayGridEffect (click an item, it scales up and neighbours translate away proportional to distance) for the hover-driven layout slot - the original triggers on click; ported to hover (mouseenter/mouseleave) per the brief's ask for a hover-driven change, noted as a substitution. All three ship GSAP (ExpandingRoundedMenu, MakeWayGridEffect) or GSAP+multiple JS modules (GridZoom: grid.js/contentItem.js/textReveal.js/textLinesReveal.js/slide-nav) - same round-1/2 answer: reimplement the mechanism in plain CSS/JS, note the drop in the table. Rejected from the shortlist: InlineMenuLayout and MenuThumbStackAnimation (both good fits too, but three is the ask; kept for a future round).
